titel: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?

einzeiler: Mathematicians discuss how artificial intelligence impacts their field and education.
kurzfassung: Recorded live at the International Congress of Mathematicians, the hosts and panel discuss how artificial intelligence is changing mathematical research, problem-solving, and proof generation. They explore whether AI threatens traditional mathematical education or serves as a powerful new tool. The conversation also highlights the human elements of mathematics, such as storytelling, intuition, and aesthetic value.
stichpunkte: AI models like AlphaProof have achieved silver and gold medals in international mathematical competitions.
Mathematicians emphasize that solving problems is only a small part of their work, alongside finding definitions and structures.
AI has successfully generated counterexamples to established conjectures, opening new avenues for human researchers.
A major concern is that students might rely on AI to do homework, hindering their foundational mental training.
Mathematics is compared to storytelling and art, relying heavily on human intuition and aesthetic appreciation.
Panelists warn that AI adoption could be used as a Trojan horse for anti-intellectualism and funding cuts in science.
Despite technological advances, the core drive for mathematical exploration remains deeply rooted in human curiosity.

clips.text: The initial success of a model solving a problem feels thrilling, but subsequent repetitions lose their novelty for both machines and students.
Technological progress risks being weaponized to justify budget reductions and discourage teaching students fundamental critical thinking skills.
Attempting to perform physical lifts while sitting inside a forklift illustrates the absurdity of misapplying automated assistance.
If all recorded human information vanished completely, artificial intelligence would cease functioning while humans would eventually restart the process.
Historical academic attitudes often degraded the vital work of surveying and exposition compared to solving original research problems.

beschreibung:
Mathematicians are witnessing a profound shift in their field. AI systems are now producing proofs, spotting connections between distant fields, and, in a few cases, solving problems that had stumped mathematicians for decades. The pace of progress over the past several months has raised challenging questions: What can AI systems actually do? And what happens to the more human, creative aspects of the field once machines can match – or exceed – people at problem-solving?
In this special live episode of The Joy of Why, recorded at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia on July 26, 2026, hosts Janna Levin and Steven Strogatz are joined by three mathematicians responding to the rise of AI in math: Akshay Venkatesh at the Institute for Advanced Study; Ravi Vakil at Stanford University and president of the American Mathematical Society; and Alex Kontorovich at Rutgers University. Together they discuss what recent AI-generated proofs really demonstrate, what will be gained and lost as mathematics becomes more machine-assisted at the frontier, and what this means for the next generation of mathematicians. The conversation turns to a deeper question: What do mathematicians value about doing mathematics in the first place? The answer involves grappling with what proof and understanding really mean, and with the surprising importance of storytelling.
untertitel: In this special live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, July 2026, the central question discussed was what do mathematicians really value about doing mathematics in the first place?
